overview: This enum selects the computer fighter's AI profile for a mission character.

None.technical: The row constructor uses None. Battle setup copies the raw byte into Setup.ByteA4 and CreateBrain passes it as AIType because only 0xFF triggers the character-row fallback. BrainCreate95 uses its default UGameCharacterBehaviorController, and the AI brain's default think node is FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CP_010.

Normal.simple: The computer fighter uses the standard CP_010 AI profile.
Normal.technical: Battle setup passes this value as AIType to CreateBrain. BrainCreate95 selects UCP_010_BehaviorController, and UGameCharacterBrain_AI::BrainInit86 selects FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CP_010.

Onslaught.simple: The computer fighter uses the CP_020 AI thinking profile.
Onslaught.technical: Battle setup passes this value as AIType to CreateBrain. BrainCreate95 has no case for it and selects the default UGameCharacterBehaviorController. UGameCharacterBrain_AI::BrainInit86 selects FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CP_020.

Invalid.simple: The fighter falls back to the AI type stored on the character row.
Invalid.technical: CreateBrain compares AIType with 0xFF and passes CharacterRow->AIType to BrainInit86 on that match. BrainCreate95 and the AI brain switch then use that replacement byte to select the behavior controller and think node.

notes: The same Operation field is copied into Setup.ByteA4 by story, arcade, PvE solo, and PvE tag battle setup.
The plain-English names describe the intent of the setting. The precise behavior comes from the CP_010 through CP_081 classes selected by the traced switches.
The read-only MissionCharacterDataTable export uses Normal, Invalid, Berserker, Unique_1, Unique_2, Carefully, Onslaught, and Shooter. None is not exported.
